source_name: CBCG — Novac u opticaju / Money in Circulation (currency section)
why_relevant: Central Bank of Montenegro's dedicated currency section covering banknotes and coins in circulation in a euroised economy. Root node for all cash-cycle sub-pages (counterfeiting protection, unfit-currency replacement, jubilee money). English mirror at /en/currency/money-in-circulation.

source_name: CBCG — Zaštita eura od falsifikovanja / Protection of Euro Banknotes and Coins against Counterfeiting
why_relevant: CBCG is the national analysis centre (NAC/CNAC equivalent) for euro counterfeits in Montenegro. Counterfeit-detection counts by denomination are periodically released (e.g. 848 counterfeit notes worth EUR 71,660 in 2024, +61.8% y/y, per Montenegrin media citing CBCG) and drive demand for detection/authentication hardware in cash handling.

source_name: CBCG — Zamjena oštećenih novčanica i kovanog novca / Replacement of Unfit Currency
why_relevant: Documents CBCG's banknote-fitness/unfit-currency replacement service — the closest Montenegrin analogue to banknote-processing/sorting operations. Useful for sizing cash-quality handling and vault/processing workload in a country that does not issue its own currency.

source_name: CBCG — Odluka o izvještajima koji se dostavljaju CBCG o platnom prometu (BUPPK reporting decision + annexes)
why_relevant: The reporting decision and its annex forms define exactly which cash/ATM/POS fields payment service providers must report quarterly (e.g. BUPPK — number of acceptance devices such as ATMs and POS terminals; separate lines for ATM cash withdrawals and cash deposits). This is the schema key that makes the published ZIP datasets interpretable, and it reveals fields that exist but are not published.

source_name: CBCG — Statistika platnog prometa: pokazatelji RTGS/DNS (monthly ZIP)
why_relevant: Monthly payment-system indicators (RTGS/DNS) plus an archived national payment transactions series through 31.12.2017. Provides the settlement-side counterpart to cash flows and lets cash withdrawal volumes be normalised against total payment turnover.

source_name: CBCG — Euroizacija / Euroisation policy page
why_relevant: CBCG's own statement of what unilateral euroisation means for its operations: it cannot control money supply, euro quantity in circulation depends on ECB policy, capital inflows, tourism, remittances and the population's propensity to hold cash. Establishes the structural reason Montenegrin cash data is fragmented and why demand drivers are external.

source_name: CBCG — Izvještaj o finansijskoj stabilnosti / Financial Stability Report
why_relevant: Financial stability reporting in a euroised system pays unusual attention to liquidity and cash holdings of banks (no ELA backstop). Useful for bank vault-cash levels and the systemic framing of cash dependence.

source_name: CBCG — Finansijski iskazi CBCG (audited financial statements)
why_relevant: Audited CBCG balance sheet discloses 'gotovina u trezoru' (cash in vault) and cash-equivalent definitions — a rare hard number on the central bank's own physical euro holdings, which is the only issuance-side quantity a euroised central bank controls.

source_name: CBCG — Saopštenja / press releases and news (aktuelno)
why_relevant: Counterfeit-statistics releases, cash-handling advisories and Council decisions surface here first and are what Montenegrin media then quote. Best early-warning feed for cash-cycle developments between annual reports.

source_name: CBCG — Radne studije (Working Papers series)
why_relevant: CBCG Research and Statistics Department working-paper series; the natural home of any Montenegrin cash-demand / cash-usage / euroisation-cost study. Confirmed to exist (e.g. Working Study no. 10 on financial-market analysis).

source_name: IMF — Montenegro country page (Article IV, Technical Assistance reports)
why_relevant: IMF staff explicitly model Montenegrin currency-in-circulation: a 2026 technical assistance report estimated seigniorage lost to unilateral euroisation using historical CiC data multiplied by an opportunity-cost proxy. That is one of the very few published CiC estimates for Montenegro and it comes with methodology.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide — investor relations / IAD network announcements
why_relevant: Independent ATM deployers are a material and growing part of Montenegro's ATM estate (tourism-driven, high-fee), and they are invisible in bank-level data. Euronet press releases and 10-K segment commentary reveal IAD market entry and network scale in Southeast Europe, which the CBCG acceptance-device counts do not attribute by operator.

source_name: RTCG — Radio Televizija Crne Gore, economy desk
why_relevant: National public broadcaster; its economy desk reports ATM fee levels (e.g. reporting EUR 3-5 withdrawal commissions as a burden on consumers) and cash-access complaints. Reveals ATM pricing and branch/ATM withdrawal behaviour that no official dataset publishes.

source_name: PV Informer / Montenegrin online media reporting CBCG counterfeit data
why_relevant: Montenegrin outlets routinely restate CBCG counterfeit findings (most-counterfeited denominations, coins included) with more detail and earlier than the consolidated annual report. Serves as a discovery layer pointing back to the underlying CBCG release.

source_name: MONSTAT — publications index (Uprava za statistiku Crne Gore)
why_relevant: Master index of Montenegrin official statistics releases; the discovery layer for tourism arrivals, retail turnover and remittance-adjacent series that drive seasonal cash demand in a euroised, tourism-heavy economy.

source_name: CBCG — Odluka o unosu i iznosu gotovine iz Crne Gore (cross-border cash declaration rules)
why_relevant: Regulation on how much cash may be brought into/out of Montenegro without declaration. In a euroised, tourism-dependent economy physical euro enters mainly through travellers and remittances, so declaration thresholds and (if published) Customs declaration totals are a genuine indirect measure of cash inflow.

source_name: ECB — Euro banknote and counterfeiting statistics (euro area issuer perspective)
why_relevant: Montenegro uses euro banknotes it does not issue, so ECB series (banknotes in circulation by denomination, semiannual counterfeit statistics, series/ES2 rollout and the future digital euro) set the physical product cycle Montenegrin cash handlers must follow. Also the benchmark against which CBCG counterfeit rates are judged.

source_name: MONSTAT — Upotreba informaciono-komunikacionih tehnologija: domaćinstva i pojedinci (ICT usage in households and by individuals)
why_relevant: The single most directly payment-relevant MONSTAT survey: annual Eurostat-aligned ICT household survey covering internet access, device use, online purchasing (e-trgovina/kupovina preko interneta) and online-payment behaviour by individuals. Supplies the e-commerce adoption denominators behind card-not-present growth. 2024 release documents 84.5% household internet access on a ~1,200-household sample.

source_name: MONSTAT — Upotreba IKT u preduzećima (ICT usage in enterprises)
why_relevant: Merchant-side counterpart to the household ICT survey: e-business, e-commerce sales, website/online-ordering capability and barriers to ICT use among Montenegrin enterprises. This is the closest official proxy for merchant acceptance readiness (which merchants can take card-not-present orders) outside the central bank's acquiring data.

source_name: MONSTAT — Promet u trgovini na malo (retail trade turnover releases)
why_relevant: Monthly/quarterly retail turnover in current and constant prices, and by commodity group (food, motor fuel, pharmaceuticals/cosmetics). This is the denominator for card-spend-to-retail-turnover penetration ratios and for judging whether card volume growth is real or price-driven. Recent releases report Q2 retail turnover +7.2% current / +4.1% constant y/y.

source_name: MONSTAT — Promet u trgovini na veliko (wholesale trade turnover)
why_relevant: Wholesale turnover complements retail as a B2B payments denominator (credit transfers, commercial cards) and helps separate consumer from business flows when interpreting aggregate payment-system value data.

source_name: MONSTAT — Turizam: dolasci i noćenja turista (tourist arrivals and overnight stays)
why_relevant: Montenegro's payment card market is structurally seasonal and foreign-cardholder-heavy; ~95.8% of 2025 overnight stays were by foreign tourists (2,728,564 arrivals / 15,367,166 overnights). Monthly arrivals and overnights by nationality are the essential normaliser for non-resident card acquiring volumes, ATM cash withdrawals in coastal municipalities and seasonal POS deployment.

source_name: MONSTAT — Anketa o potrošnji domaćinstava (Household Budget Survey)
why_relevant: Household income, expenditure and consumption structure by COICOP purpose — the demand-side base for consumer payment capacity, wallet share by category and cash-intensity of spending categories. Conducted since 1983; since 2015 on a multi-year cycle (roughly every 2-3 years) with 1100/380-household samples, so cadence is low but structural value is high.
